purpose: Wire TOPA's artifact-classifier lane into the wider TOPA organism without contaminating supervised image-forensics labels with unrelated repository text.
what_repo_assimilation_means: TOPA indexes its own methods and schemas
TOPA preserves and rediscovers failed and negative runs
TOPA discovers preregistrations and frozen gates
TOPA discovers source ledgers and provenance routes
TOPA discovers JANUS integration and swarm routing paths
TOPA routes artifact-classifier-relevant files into a dedicated investigation queue
what_repo_assimilation_does_not_mean: Repository prose is not image ground truth
Historical claims are not promoted to facts
P versus NP or Hessdalen files do not become POSS-I classifier labels
Nuclear context cannot enter artifact-classifier fitting
A repo scan alone cannot improve or validate classifier accuracy

training_split.organism_training: Repository assimilation acts as methodological and investigative memory: methods, failures, confounders, source routes and epistemic rules become searchable context.
training_split.artifact_classifier_training: Separately admitted blind image labels plus measured POSS-I feature rails are used for supervised fitting.
training_split.reason_for_firewall: Prevents unrelated project lore, historical hypotheses or downstream nuclear results from contaminating the image-forensics target.

claim_ceiling: TOPA is now wired to assimilate its own repository as research memory while keeping the artifact classifier scientifically isolated. The first full repository CI scan must pass before claiming the assimilation run itself executed successfully.
